newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, retail flows sluggish.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip, retail flows sluggish.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities plodded lower on Monday, mainly tracking Treasuries, mortgage experts said.
With little support from retail buying, yield spreads held largely unchanged, traders said.
Late in the afternoon, mortgages had fallen 1/32 to 4/32 overall, while comparable Treasuries were off 2/32 to 4/32.

"It's been very quiet today," one trader said. Many market players were looking ahead to the second installment of Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday, as well as Friday's employment report, he said.
In specific coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was off 3/32 at 99-24/32, yielding 97 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mae issues had slipped 3/32 as well, to 99-22/32 and 99-27/32, respectively.
The 10-year note was off 2/32 at 97-23/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
A key manufacturing-sector survey by the National Association of Purchasing Managers added to the fixed-income markets' bearish opening tone, analysts said.
NAPM's February index read 53.1, up from 52.0 the month before.
Some economists took the news as a sign of industry strength going into Friday's payrolls report.

In a Reuters survey last Friday, economists projected a payrolls gain of 230,000 and an unemployment rate of 5.3 percent. That compares with 271,000 new jobs and a 5.4 percent jobless rate in January.
